  • Method Details

    • bindCertificate

      @RequestMapping(method=POST, value="/api/account/certificates", produces={"application/json","application/problem+json"}, consumes="application/json") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Certificate> bindCertificate(@Valid @RequestBody @Valid BindCertificateRequest bindCertificateRequest)
      POST /api/account/certificates : Binds a certificate Binds the X.509 certificate of the request, in PEM form, to the authenticated account, so it can sign in with it. Only the public certificate is sent, never its private key. The certificate is recognised by the SHA-256 fingerprint of its DER form, never by its subject; it must be within its validity period. Binding a certificate the account already has answers the existing binding. While the account has a confirmed second factor, the bearer token must show a recent multi-factor sign-in (step-up, RFC 9470).
      Parameters:
      bindCertificateRequest - (required)
      Returns:
      The certificate is bound (or was already bound to the account) (status code 201) or The request is invalid, or the value is not a single PEM X.509 certificate within its validity period (problem type urn:problem:certificate:invalid-certificate) (status code 400) or Missing or invalid bearer token (an RFC 6750 challenge and no body), or the account has a confirmed second factor and the token does not show a multi-factor sign-in (acr urn:irurueta:acr:mfa) whose auth_time is within authserver.mfa.step-up-max-age (default 5 minutes). The latter is answered as RFC 9470 describes, with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error=\"insufficient_user_authentication\", acr_values=\"urn:irurueta:acr:mfa\", max_age=\"300\" (the configured age in seconds) and a problem body; the client signs the user in again with those acr_values and max_age and retries with the new token. (status code 401) or The certificate is bound to another account (problem type urn:problem:certificate:certificate-already-bound) (status code 409)

    • listCertificates

      @RequestMapping(method=GET, value="/api/account/certificates", produces="application/json") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<List<Certificate>> listCertificates()
      GET /api/account/certificates : Lists the bound certificates Lists the X.509 client certificates bound to the authenticated account, oldest first, never anything of another account. A bound certificate signs the account in on POST /login/x509 when authserver.x509.enabled is true.
      Returns:
      The bound certificates (status code 200) or Missing or invalid bearer token (status code 401)

    • unbindCertificate

      @RequestMapping(method=DELETE, value="/api/account/certificates/{id}", produces="application/problem+json") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> unbindCertificate(@PathVariable("id") UUID id)
      DELETE /api/account/certificates/{id} : Unbinds a certificate The certificate can no longer be used to sign in. A certificate of another account is never touched and is answered as not found. While the account has a confirmed second factor, the bearer token must show a recent multi-factor sign-in (step-up, RFC 9470). The last way to sign in to the account is never removed: a certificate is refused while the account has neither a password nor a linked identity, a passkey or another certificate.
      Parameters:
      id - Identifier of the binding. (required)
      Returns:
      Certificate unbound (status code 204) or Missing or invalid bearer token (an RFC 6750 challenge and no body), or the account has a confirmed second factor and the token does not show a multi-factor sign-in (acr urn:irurueta:acr:mfa) whose auth_time is within authserver.mfa.step-up-max-age (default 5 minutes). The latter is answered as RFC 9470 describes, with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error=\"insufficient_user_authentication\", acr_values=\"urn:irurueta:acr:mfa\", max_age=\"300\" (the configured age in seconds) and a problem body; the client signs the user in again with those acr_values and max_age and retries with the new token. (status code 401) or No such certificate for the authenticated account (problem type urn:problem:certificate:certificate-not-found) (status code 404) or The certificate is the last way to sign in to the account (problem type urn:problem:certificate:last-sign-in-method) (status code 409)
